newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asia naphtha buyers ask ADNOC to distinguish price.
newsitem.headline: Asia naphtha buyers ask ADNOC to distinguish price.

text.p: Asian naphtha buyers have asked the Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) to set separate prices for two different types of naphtha for annual term contracts starting in July, traders said on Tuesday.
ADNOC has in the past sold both pentane-plus naphtha, which is paraffinic naphtha favoured as feedstock for ethylene production, and full-range "low sulphur" naphtha at the same price.
In the oil products market, traders usually assess the price of full-range naphtha at a discount of $2.00 to $3.00 per tonne to paraffinic naphtha.
Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil firm Saudi Aramco recently set the term premium for paraffinic A-180 naphtha at $17.00 a tonne and $15.00 for full-range Jubail naphtha for the one year starting July.
Traders said different prices for the two grades of naphtha would be favourable for buyers.
ADNOC's reaction to the proposal, however, would not become clear until the two sides meet for term contract negotiations in the first week of June in Abu Dhabi, they said.
ADNOC has already notified potential customers of its initial offer price of $22.50 over the ADNOC formula for the new term year starting in July, compared with a $6.80 premium the previous year.
Potential Asian buyers -- one South Korean petrochemical firm, three Japanese trading houses and one Japanese oil firm -- would not comment on their initial bidding levels.
Some traders said they expected buyers to have placed bids in the "high teens". --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
